title: Topic Drill: Data, Probability and Statistics (Set A)

items.stem:
A bookmobile logged the books borrowed at four stops on Tuesday.
Stop | Books borrowed
Mill Road | 34
Oak Court | 27
Harbor Lane | 41
Fern Street | 22
How many more books were borrowed at the busiest stop than at the quietest stop?
items.explanation: The busiest stop is Harbor Lane with 41 books, and the quietest is Fern Street with 22 books. The difference is 41 minus 22 equals 19. The value 14 compares the busiest stop with Oak Court, which is not the quietest. The value 7 compares two middle stops, and 63 adds the extremes rather than subtracting them.

items.stem: A hatchery weighed 40 trout. Twelve weighed under 10 ounces, 20 weighed from 10 to 14 ounces, and 8 weighed over 14 ounces. What percent of the trout weighed at least 10 ounces?
items.explanation: Trout of at least 10 ounces include the middle group and the heaviest group: 20 + 8 equals 28 of 40, which is 70 percent. The value 30 is the percent weighing under 10 ounces (12 of 40), the complement of the answer. The value 50 counts only the middle group, and 20 counts only the heaviest group, so each leaves out part of the data asked about.

items.stem:
A lab inspects small batches and records the number of defects found. The table shows the probabilities.
Defects | Probability
0 | 0.5
1 | 0.3
2 | 0.2
What is the expected number of defects per batch?
items.explanation: Multiply each value by its probability and add: 0 times 0.5 plus 1 times 0.3 plus 2 times 0.2 equals 0.7. The value 1 is the simple average of 0, 1 and 2, which ignores the probabilities. The value 0.5 is the largest probability, belonging to the most likely outcome, not the average. The value 2 is the largest number of defects, which is the maximum, not the expected value.

items.stem: A band student’s mean score on five music-theory quizzes is 82. After a sixth quiz, the mean of all six scores is 84. What score did the student earn on the sixth quiz?
items.explanation: Five quizzes at a mean of 82 total 410 points. Six quizzes at a mean of 84 total 504 points. The sixth score is the difference, 504 minus 410 equals 94. The value 84 assumes the new score equals the new mean, and 2 is only how much the mean rose. The value 504 is the total of all six scores, not the sixth score alone.

items.stem: Four band members will each play one solo, one after another. In how many different orders can the four solos be performed?
items.explanation: The first solo has 4 choices, the next 3, then 2, then 1, so the count is 4 times 3 times 2 times 1 equals 24. The value 16 allows a member to be repeated, 4 times 4, though each member plays only once. The value 12 stops after two positions, and 10 adds 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 instead of multiplying them.

items.stem: At the lighthouse museum, 5 of every 20 visitors buy a $6 poster, and the others buy no poster. What is the expected poster spending per visitor, in dollars?
items.explanation: The probability of buying is 5 over 20, which is 1/4. Expected spending is 1/4 times 6 equals 1.50 dollars per visitor. The value 6 is the price paid by a buyer, not the average across all visitors. The value 30 is the total for the five buyers in a group of 20, and 0.25 is only the probability of buying.

items.stem: A community college lab weighs five soil samples in grams: 20, 22, 23, 24 and 26. Then a sixth sample of 80 grams is added. Which statement correctly compares the mean and the median of the six values with the original five?
options: The mean stays at 23, while the median rises to 32.5
The mean and the median both rise to 32.5
The mean rises to 23.5, while the median rises to 32.5
The mean rises from 23 to 32.5, while the median rises only from 23 to 23.5
items.explanation: Originally the mean is 115 divided by 5 equals 23 and the median is 23. With 80 added, the sum is 195, so the mean is 195 divided by 6 equals 32.5. The ordered list has 23 and 24 in the middle, so the median is 23.5. An outlier drags the mean strongly but moves the median little, so the other choices swap or misreport the two measures.

items.stem: Six trout at a hatchery weigh 14, 15, 16, 16, 17 and 18 ounces. A seventh trout weighing 30 ounces is added. By how many ounces does the range increase?
items.explanation: The original range is 18 minus 14 equals 4 ounces. With the 30-ounce trout, the range is 30 minus 14 equals 16 ounces, so it increases by 12. The value 4 is the original range, 16 is the new range rather than the increase, and 30 is the new maximum, which is not a range at all. One outlier can change the range sharply because it uses only the two extreme values.

items.stem: A seed bank shipped 200 packets in February. Shipments rose by 50 percent in March and then fell by 50 percent in April. How many packets were shipped in April?
items.explanation: A 50 percent rise on 200 gives 200 + 100 equals 300 packets in March. The April drop is 50 percent of 300, which is 150, so April shipments are 300 minus 150 equals 150. The value 200 assumes equal and opposite percents cancel, though they apply to different bases. The value 250 subtracts 50 packets instead of 50 percent. The value 300 is the March figure, ignoring the drop.

items.stem: A tutoring center has 6 tutors and needs to choose 2 of them to staff a help desk. The order of the two chosen does not matter. How many different pairs are possible?
items.explanation: Choosing 2 from 6 gives 6 times 5 equals 30 ordered pairs, and each pair is counted twice, so divide by 2 to get 15. The value 30 leaves out the division by 2 and treats the order as important. The value 12 multiplies 6 by 2, and 8 adds 6 + 2, which are not valid counting methods for pairs.

items.stem: A seed bank customer picks one of 5 seed varieties, one of 4 pot sizes and one of 3 soil mixes. How many different combinations of variety, pot size and soil mix are possible?
items.explanation: By the counting principle, multiply the number of choices at each step: 5 times 4 times 3 equals 60. The value 12 adds the three numbers, which counts the individual items instead of the combinations. The value 20 multiplies only variety and pot size and leaves out the soil mix. The value 15 multiplies variety and soil mix and leaves out the pot size.

items.stem: A hatchery technician screens one tank twice with independent tests. Each test has a 0.1 probability of showing a disease signal. What is the probability that at least one test shows the signal?
items.explanation: The complement of at least one is none. No signal in either test has probability 0.9 times 0.9 equals 0.81, so at least one has probability 1 minus 0.81 equals 0.19. The value 0.81 is the chance of none, 0.01 is the chance of both, and 0.2 adds the two probabilities, which double counts the case in which both tests show the signal.

items.stem: A jar holds 5 red, 7 blue and 8 green marbles. One marble is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is not blue?
items.explanation: There are 20 marbles, and 5 + 8 equals 13 are not blue, so the probability is 13/20. Equivalently, 1 minus 7/20 equals 13/20. The fraction 7/20 is the probability of drawing blue. The fraction 13/7 compares non-blue with blue marbles, giving a value above 1, which cannot be a probability. The fraction 2/5 counts only the green marbles.

items.stem: A lighthouse museum counted visitors over one weekend: 70 on Friday, 120 on Saturday and 110 on Sunday. What fraction of the weekend’s visitors came on Saturday?
items.explanation: The total is 70 + 120 + 110 equals 300 visitors, and Saturday accounts for 120, so the fraction is 120 over 300, which simplifies to 2/5. The fraction 3/5 is the share on the other two days. The fraction 1/3 assumes the visitors were spread evenly over three days, and 12/11 compares Saturday only with Sunday instead of with the whole weekend.

items.stem: After 50 people leaving the lighthouse museum’s gift shop were surveyed, the director announced that 80 percent of all town residents enjoy the new exhibit. What is the main weakness of this claim?
options: Fifty people is too few to compute any percent
Eighty percent is too large to be a real survey result
The percent should have been found out of 100 people, not 50
The people surveyed were all museum visitors, so they may not represent all town residents
items.explanation: A claim about all residents needs a sample that represents all residents. Visitors leaving a museum shop are likely to enjoy the museum, so the sample is biased, and a larger biased sample would not fix this. Fifty people can still give a percent (40 out of 50 is 80 percent), and any percent from 0 to 100 is possible, so the other explanations name no real flaw.

items.stem: Members of a school band logged practice minutes for one week: 40, 20, 35, 20, 55, 30, 20 and 45. What is the range of the practice times, in minutes?
items.explanation: The range is the largest value minus the smallest: 55 minus 20 equals 35 minutes. The value 55 reports only the maximum, and 75 adds the two extremes instead of subtracting them. The value 37.5 is their average, the midrange, which locates the center of the extremes rather than the spread. The mode, 20, is also not the range.

items.stem: A hatchery tray yields 40 healthy fry with probability 0.7 and 20 healthy fry with probability 0.3. What is the expected number of healthy fry per tray?
items.explanation: Expected value is 40 times 0.7 plus 20 times 0.3, which is 28 + 6 equals 34 fry. The value 30 averages 40 and 20 and ignores the unequal probabilities. The value 28 includes only the more likely outcome. The value 60 adds the two yields, treating both as certain to happen, which cannot occur on a single tray.

items.stem: Volunteers counted 240 birds at a wetland, and 60 of them were sparrows. What percent of the birds counted were sparrows?
items.explanation: Percent equals part over whole times 100, so 60 divided by 240 equals 1/4, which is 25 percent. The value 4 inverts the ratio, dividing 240 by 60. The value 75 is the percent that were not sparrows, and 180 is the number of birds that were not sparrows, which is a count instead of a percent. Each wrong value responds to a different question than the one asked.

items.stem: A seed bank shelf holds 60 packets, and 18 of them are tomato seeds. If one packet is chosen at random, what is the probability that it holds tomato seeds?
items.explanation: Probability is favorable outcomes over total outcomes: 18 over 60 simplifies to 3/10. The fraction 3/7 compares tomato packets with the 42 other packets, which gives odds instead of probability. The fraction 7/10 is the probability of choosing a packet that is not tomato, and 1/18 divides one by the number of tomato packets instead of counting favorable outcomes over total outcomes.

items.stem:
A tutoring center logged visits by subject and time of day.
Subject | Morning | Evening
Math | 14 | 16
Reading | 22 | 18
Writing | 12 | 18
What percent of all visits took place in the evening?
items.explanation: Add the evening column: 16 + 18 + 18 equals 52. The morning column adds to 14 + 22 + 12 equals 48, so the total is 100 and the evening share is 52 percent. The value 48 is the morning share. The value 34 leaves out the Writing row, and the value 18 reads a single cell instead of the whole column.

items.stem: A hatchery manager has 5 tanks and will inspect 4 of them today, in any order. How many different sets of 4 tanks can be chosen?
items.explanation: Choosing 4 tanks to inspect is the same as choosing the 1 tank to skip, and there are 5 ways to do that, so the answer is 5. The value 20 multiplies 5 by 4, counting ordered pairs. The value 120 counts ordered arrangements of 4 from 5, 5 times 4 times 3 times 2. The value 9 adds 5 + 4, which does not count sets at all.

items.stem: In a probability lesson at the tutoring center, a student flips a fair coin four times in a row. How many different sequences of heads and tails are possible?
items.explanation: Each flip has 2 outcomes and the flips are independent, so the counting principle gives 2 times 2 times 2 times 2 equals 16 sequences. The value 8 multiplies 2 by 4 instead of using 2 four times. The value 6 adds 2 + 4. The value 24 is the number of ways to arrange four distinct items, which does not describe flip results with only two outcomes each.

items.stem: On a given morning, the lighthouse museum’s tour guide arrives on time with probability 3/4, and the elevator works with probability 2/3. If these events are independent, what is the probability that both happen?
items.explanation: Multiply independent probabilities: 3/4 times 2/3 equals 6/12, which simplifies to 1/2. The fraction 17/12 adds them and is larger than 1. The fraction 1/12 subtracts them, 3/4 minus 2/3, which has no meaning here. The fraction 2/3 is simply the smaller of the two probabilities, which would be correct only if a working elevator guaranteed the guide arrived.

items.stem:
A tutoring center recorded how many times each of 20 students visited last week.
Visits | Students
1 | 4
2 | 6
3 | 8
4 | 2
What is the mean number of visits per student?
items.explanation: Multiply each visit count by its number of students: 1 times 4, 2 times 6, 3 times 8 and 4 times 2 give 4 + 12 + 24 + 8 equals 48 visits. Dividing by 20 students gives 2.4. The value 2.5 averages the four visit counts without weighting, 3 is the mode, and 12 divides 48 by the four rows instead of the 20 students.

items.stem: A birdwatching club installed a new feeder in April. Sightings rose from 30 per week in March to 45 per week in April. The club claims the feeder caused the 15 extra sightings. Which statement best evaluates the claim?
options: The claim is proven, because 45 is greater than 30
The claim is false, because a feeder cannot change bird counts
The claim is proven, because 15 is half of the March count
The data show a rise, but spring migration or other factors could also explain it, so a cause is not established
items.explanation: Two numbers measured before and after show that sightings rose, but they do not isolate the reason. April is also when many species migrate, so the increase could have happened without the feeder. A comparison with a similar location lacking a feeder would be stronger evidence. Saying the claim is proven because 45 is larger than 30, or because 15 is half of 30, mistakes a rise for a cause.

items.stem: At a rural stop, the bookmobile gets 8 visitors on one quarter of its trips and 4 visitors on the other three quarters of its trips. What is the expected number of visitors per trip?
items.explanation: Weight each outcome by its probability: 8 times 1/4 equals 2, and 4 times 3/4 equals 3, so the expected value is 2 + 3 equals 5 visitors. The value 6 is the plain average of 8 and 4, which ignores that the smaller turnout is three times as common. The value 12 adds 8 and 4, and 3 counts only the contribution of the 4-visitor trips.

items.stem: A clarinet player knows that each new reed is playable with probability 3/5, independent of any other reed. Two new reeds are taken from a box. What is the probability that both are playable?
items.explanation: For independent events, multiply the probabilities: 3/5 times 3/5 equals 9/25. The fraction 6/5 adds the two probabilities, which exceeds 1 and cannot be a probability. The fraction 3/5 gives the chance for a single reed and ignores the second one. The fraction 6/25 multiplies 3 by 2 in the numerator, using the number of reeds instead of the second probability of 3/5.

items.stem: During a winter bird count, volunteers recorded the number of cardinals seen at eight feeders: 13, 7, 22, 9, 15, 11, 18 and 9. What is the median number of cardinals per feeder?
items.explanation: Order the values: 7, 9, 9, 11, 13, 15, 18, 22. With eight values, the median is the mean of the fourth and fifth, (11 + 13) divided by 2 equals 12. The value 9 is the mode, the most frequent value. The value 11 is only the fourth value, and 13 is the mean of all eight values (104 divided by 8), so neither is the middle of the ordered list.

items.stem: A seed bank holds 80 samples, and 15 percent are flagged for review. Of the flagged samples, three quarters are rechecked this week. How many samples are rechecked this week?
items.explanation: Flagged samples are 15 percent of 80, which is 12. Three quarters of 12 is 9. The value 12 stops after finding the flagged group. The value 60 takes three quarters of all 80 samples, skipping the 15 percent step. The value 3 finds the quarter that is not rechecked rather than the three quarters that are.

items.stem: A band director surveys 48 members. Exactly 3/8 of the members play brass, and 1/3 of the brass players play trombone. How many members play trombone?
items.explanation: Brass players are 3/8 of 48, which is 18. Trombone players are 1/3 of those 18, which is 6. The value 18 stops after the first step. The value 16 takes 1/3 of all 48 members and skips the brass group. The value 34 adds the two fractions, 3/8 + 1/3 equals 17/24, and takes that part of 48, which treats the fractions as separate groups instead of nested ones.

items.stem:
A bookmobile counted its riders in one week.
Rider group | Riders
Child | 25
Teen | 15
Adult | 40
Senior | 20
If one rider is chosen at random, what is the probability that the rider is a child or a senior?
items.explanation: Total riders are 25 + 15 + 40 + 20 equals 100. Children and seniors together are 25 + 20 equals 45, so the probability is 45/100, which simplifies to 9/20. The fraction 1/4 includes only children and 1/5 includes only seniors. The fraction 11/20 is the probability of a rider who is a teen or an adult, the complement of the event asked about.

items.stem: A regional seed bank logs the number of new seed packets processed each weekday: 5, 8, 9, 12 and 16. What is the mean number of packets processed per day?
items.explanation: The mean is the sum divided by the count: 5 + 8 + 9 + 12 + 16 equals 50, and 50 divided by 5 days equals 10 packets. The value 9 is the median, the middle number, not the mean. The value 11 is the range, 16 minus 5. The value 50 is the total with the final division left out, so it does not describe a typical day.

items.stem:
The lighthouse museum recorded daily visitors Monday to Friday.
Day | Visitors
Monday | 44
Tuesday | 38
Wednesday | 38
Thursday | 52
Friday | 58
What is the mean number of visitors per day?
items.explanation: The five days total 44 + 38 + 38 + 52 + 58 equals 230 visitors, and 230 divided by 5 equals 46. The value 38 is the mode, the most common daily count. The value 44 is the median, the middle value of the ordered list 38, 38, 44, 52, 58. The value 230 is the total with the division by 5 left out.

items.stem: Three picture books with different colored covers are placed on a bookmobile shelf in a random order. What is the probability that they land in one specific order chosen in advance?
items.explanation: Three books can be arranged in 3 times 2 times 1 equals 6 ways, and only one of them is the chosen order, so the probability is 1/6. The fraction 1/3 is the chance that one particular book comes first, which fixes only one position. The fractions 1/9 and 1/27 let each position use any of the 3 books again, as if books could repeat.

items.stem: A tutoring center timed six sessions, in minutes: 20, 25, 30, x, 45 and 50, listed in order. The median of the six times is 35. What is the value of x?
items.explanation: With six values, the median is the mean of the third and fourth: (30 + x) divided by 2 equals 35, so 30 + x equals 70 and x equals 40. The value 70 is the sum 30 + x before the last step. The value 35 assumes the missing time equals the median, and 5 is the gap between 35 and 30, which forgets that the median is an average of two values.

items.stem: A tutoring center advertises that its average group size is 6 students. A parent concludes that no group ever has more than 6 students. Which response best evaluates this conclusion?
options: It is justified, because the average cannot be less than the largest group
It is justified, because the mean always equals the most common group size
It is unjustified, because an average can only describe groups of exactly 6
It is unjustified, because an average of 6 allows some groups to be larger than 6 and others smaller
items.explanation: An average balances values above and below it, so groups of 8 can exist alongside groups of 4 and still average 6. For example, sizes 4, 6 and 8 have a mean of 6 and a largest group of 8. The mean never equals the maximum unless every group is the same size, and the mean need not equal the mode either, so the other responses misstate how averages work.

items.stem: At a community college lab, a sample passes a quality check with probability 0.92. What is the probability that a randomly chosen sample fails the check?
items.explanation: Failing is the complement of passing, so the probability is 1 minus 0.92 equals 0.08. The value 0.92 is the probability of passing, not failing. The value 8 converts 0.08 to a percent but drops the percent sign, which mixes decimals and percents. The value 0.18 comes from a subtraction slip, 1 minus 0.82, which gives the wrong complement.

items.stem: A fish hatchery counted 160 fertilized eggs in its first tray and 200 in its second tray. The second tray has what percent more eggs than the first tray?
items.explanation: The difference is 200 minus 160 equals 40 eggs. Percent more is measured against the first tray: 40 divided by 160 equals 25 percent. The value 20 divides by the larger tray, 200, which is the wrong base. The value 40 is the raw difference, not a percent, and 125 is the second tray as a percent of the first, which includes the original 100 percent.

items.stem: A lighthouse museum has 5 artifacts and 3 display cases in a row. Each case holds one artifact, and no artifact is used twice. How many different ways can the cases be filled?
items.explanation: Order matters because the cases are different positions. The first case has 5 choices, the second 4 and the third 3, so the total is 5 times 4 times 3 equals 60. The value 10 counts groups of 3 artifacts without order. The value 20 stops after two cases, and 15 multiplies 5 by 3, skipping the second case.

items.stem: A fish hatchery recorded fry counts, in hundreds, for four weeks: 30, 36, 28 and 34. The hatchery wants the five-week mean to be 33. How many hundreds of fry are needed in week five?
items.explanation: A mean of 33 over five weeks needs a total of 5 times 33 equals 165. The first four weeks add to 128, so week five must supply 165 minus 128 equals 37. The value 4 comes from using four weeks, 132, instead of five. The value 33 assumes the missing week equals the mean, and 165 is the required total, not the missing part.
